title: AbyssReader server kit import manifest
description: What `abyssreader-server admin import <folder>` reads from <folder>/manifest.json. The kit never crawls: the operator writes this file. Every title has an operator-chosen stable `ref`, so importing again updates the title instead of adding a second one. An import never deletes a title (`admin titles remove <ref>` does). manifestVersion 1 may gain optional fields (such as hosted titles); anything a kit of manifestVersion 1 could misread gets a new manifestVersion.

$comment.description: Free text; the import ignores it.

manifestVersion.description: The format's version. This kit reads 1.

sources.description: Sources the titles' source titles point to. A source imported earlier need not be listed again; a listed one is updated to what is listed here.

sourceSlug.description: A source's slug, as the contract's SourceSlug.

lang.description: A language code (en, es, pt-BR), as the contract's LangCode.

filePath.description: A file in the manifest's folder: a relative path with / separators that stays inside the folder.

hostedSourceTitle.description: One language of a hosted title: its reader hint, its rights and its chapters. Chapters (or languages) the entry no longer lists are removed only by `admin import --remove-chapters`; otherwise they are kept and reported.

readingMode.description: The reader's default for this source title; the user's own setting wins. Absent or null: none.

rights.description: Licence and credit facts, shown in the app as they are. Absent or null: none. A field left out is null.

licence.description: Free text, for example CC BY 4.0.

chapter.description: One hosted chapter. Its ref is the operator's stable key inside its hosted source title: a second import with the same ref updates the chapter and keeps its id, which the app's reading marks and sync rely on.

publishedAt.description: A date (2026-11-20, midnight UTC) or a UTC time (2026-11-20T10:00:00Z). Absent: the time of the import that first added the chapter.

credits.description: Who made or translated this chapter, as free text.

pages.description: The page files in reading order (plain files in this folder): JPEG, PNG or still WebP, at most 2000 px wide and 60 000 px tall; a page is at most 6000 px tall and 5 MiB, and a taller page is cut into slices at import. A chapter is served as at most 500 images. width and height, each when given, must be the file's own.

website.description: The source website as an https origin with no path. It identifies the source across servers (backups match by it).

iconUrl.description: The source's icon, served to the app as it is (absolute https, loadable with no headers).

tachiyomiIds.description: The Mihon/Tachiyomi source ids of this source, as decimal strings for backup matching. Import requires a positive signed 64-bit integer (at most 9223372036854775807) and treats aliases that differ only by leading zeroes as the same id.

ref.description: The operator's stable reference for this title. A second import with the same ref updates the title. Merging sources into one title is listing them under one ref; the kit never guesses.

slug.description: The title's slug in the app's links (GET /api/v1/titles/by-slug/{slug}); unique on the server. Default: the ref.

genres.description: Genre names. A genre is matched by its slug (lower-cased letters and digits, other characters as dashes), so "Slice of Life" and "slice-of-life" are one genre.

year.description: The title's first publication year. A missing or null year is unknown. This is stored in the kit catalog only.

rating.description: The title's rating from 0 to 10, from a source of the operator's choice; null or absent when unrated.

coverUrl.description: An https URL the import downloads into the server's storage. If it fails, the title is imported without a cover and `admin covers retry` tries again.

coverFile.description: A JPEG, PNG or WebP file in the manifest's folder, instead of coverUrl.

hosted.description: The title's chapters hosted on this server (the optional feature hosted-chapters): one hosted source title per language. A title has sourceTitles, hosted, or both. The import keeps a hosted source title's id while its lang stays the same. An entry without hosted leaves the title's hosted chapters as they are.

sourceTitles.description: The title on each source that offers it. A source title belongs to one title; the import keeps its id while its source and url stay the same. The slug `hosted` is the server's own hosted source and cannot be named here.

url.description: Its address on the source: a root-relative path on the source's website, or an absolute http(s) URL, as the source's definition expects it.
